original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: On PR2979's words (Marius-Paul Dumitrean: PR2942 plus joint codimension-2 end-frame lowering of 22 restored helpers to five shared rank-7 subspaces, five further rank-8 paired extractions at normals 42 and 7 with 91 private buffers, and Jeremy Kothe's fourteen PR2957 rewrites) and PR3015's declared literal edit stage (Jeremy Kothe): two declared restore edit blocks (R1_E42 on restore[162:188] and R2_E7 on restore[190:203]) routing pivot transfers through partner carriers (369, 450, 19) and pivot 363 as self-carrier so six registers (63, 54, 40, 22, 73, 5) skip their intermediate rank-8 hyperplane (E_42 or E_7) and climb 7 -> 9 (-12 H1 + 6 H2 per call) at unchanged width inventory and literal T74 allocation, with complete fresh-native admission and modern outer release.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a changed helper inventory or local cost interface beats current packing. PR2979 introduced the 91-buffer six-width-class inventory and its literal T74 allocation, and PR3015 introduced a declared restore-edit stage showing that carrier routing lets register 63 skip E_42. Here we extend that restore-edit stage to all five stage-2 normal-42 and normal-7 restore blocks via two declared edit blocks (R1_E42 and R2_E7), achieving six rank-8 hyperplane skips at unchanged helper widths and buffer count, and verify complete fresh-native admission and outer release.
bottleneck_link: Six registers (63, 54, 40 at E_42; 22, 73, 5 at E_7) skip their intermediate rank-8 restore hyperplane and climb directly 7 -> 9 via partner carriers (369, 450, 19) and pivot 363 as self-carrier, lowering the per-call local profile by -12 H1 + 6 H2 (-29,826 units/call) from PR2979's {1:2445, 2:706, 3:232, 4:108, 5:18, 8:8} to {1:2433, 2:712, 3:232, 4:108, 5:18, 8:8} at the same width inventory {4:26, 5:2, 6:16, 7:52, 8:99, 9:213} and 91 private buffers. The fixed-capacity cap rises to 0.001729737950064278551242 and the certified literal release reaches 0.001729736166387915986812 - 10^-46 - 10^-70 (+7.022e-7 above PR2979).
stop_rule: Freeze the declared restore edits after exact local checks and 11-control per-word tamper review; publish a higher conditional kappa only if both native providers, literal owner geometry, physical stock, prefix and complete outer admission pass strictly above the PR2979 and PR2969 headlines.
evidence: Checks: run_registered.py (stdlib): package pins; verify.py (PR2979 producer reconstruction of every stage word, stage-1 validity, five structure certificates per provider, PR2833 auditor forward/dual on every stage word, frame accounting, 86 semantic controls, price evidence, overlay spec round trip); edits/edits_review.py (pure declared-edit applier for R1_E42 and R2_E7, PR2833 auditor forward/dual over all 632 inputs on both edited final words, and 11 semantic tamper controls per word); check_allocation.py (owner engine, five controls, physical 66,813, exact moment vs PR2969); check_cap.py (Fractions-only caps of the parent, every stage, and the edited final profile, recorded literal gap 1.7837e-9, exact gains over PR2979/PR2969/PR2966/PR2957/PR2942); stored receipts binding. reproduce.py: exact Git exports of PR2908/PR2917/PR2942/PR2957/PR2966/PR2969 (and through them PR2894/PR2833), authenticated retained cache, PR2917 derived source plus the rank7-joint-endframes stage and the declared-edit-stage (manifest 130650ad), 91-buffer adapters, fresh native chains for both providers and complete admission: PASS_REPLICA_ORDER_FILL_DERIVATIVE_COMPLETE_RELEASE and PASS_RELEASE at the claimed kappa.

open_questions.question: Do lowerings by one dimension of the five new pivots and their partners, or of other restored groups, pay on the final words?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Stage 1 used every restored helper whose solver lower bound left room (20 + 4 candidates); stage 2 created five new restored endpoints at E_42 and E_7 whose end frames have not been censused for a shared rank-7 subspace.
open_questions.first_step: Run the lower-bound census (end frame vs L_h) on the final word, group candidates by common W and price each group jointly with the certified frame solver.
open_questions.blocked_by: Each new group needs its own frame-edit record and the full exact/admission chain.

open_questions.question: Can normals 25 and 52 be used with pivots other than 363?
open_questions.why_it_matters: On the stage-1 word normals 25 and 52 had +20,766 margins at k = 2, but they reuse pivots 363 and 395 of normal 7; after stage 2 normal 52 has pairing rank 0 and normal 25 is at -34,529.
open_questions.first_step: Re-run kopt on the stage-1 word with 363 and 395 excluded, and compose any positive normal-25/52 set in all orders with normal 7 and 42.

open_questions.question: Can the changed inventory be packed closer to its cap?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The cap basis is fractional at T74 (denominators 4 and 20); the literal fill is below the cap by the gap recorded in check_cap.py.
open_questions.first_step: Solve the chronological flow directly at T74 or at a multiple of T where the basic counts are integral, keeping the interval Hall condition for width-7 roles.
open_questions.blocked_by: Integrality of the basic solution at T74 and the chronology (interval Hall) constraint.
